title: Senior Pharmacist: Interpret a Near-Miss Reporting Pilot
prompt: You are a senior pharmacist advising fictional Larch Service on a handoff pilot. Supplied four-week table: Site A before: 8 near-miss reports / 800 collections; after: 18 / 900. Site B before: 6 / 600; after: 7 / 700. Only A introduced a simpler reporting form and protected reporting time. The project slide says, "The pilot made A less safe: cancel it." Reporting completeness and independently reviewed incident severity were not measured. Review the claim and propose a six-week learning plan. Exercise policy requires potential patient concerns to be reviewed by the designated clinical lead independently of the analytics review. Do not infer clinical harm or design medicine-handling procedures.
blurb: Separate reporting changes from safety outcomes and design a modest, auditable learning plan.

rubric.label: Interpret the denominators and reporting change
rubric.description: Computes or explains rates without mistaking reports for harm.

anchors.0: Uses the raw increase from 8 to 18 as proof of doubled harm.
anchors.2: Identifies A's reporting rate change from 1% to 2% and B's stable 1%.
anchors.4: Explains that a reporting intervention can alter ascertainment and that neither rates nor the comparison establish harm, benefit, or causality without completeness/severity information.

rubric.label: Specify useful evidence
rubric.description: Creates a feasible way to test competing explanations.

anchors.0: Declares success or failure without additional evidence.
anchors.2: Proposes reviewing cases and measuring reporting completeness.
anchors.4: Defines a six-week sample review with consistent definitions, independent clinical classification, comparable exposure counts, reporting participation, and criteria to revise or stop the pilot if reviewed concerns emerge.

rubric.label: Separate immediate review from aggregate learning
rubric.description: Keeps individual concerns owned while avoiding punitive reporting incentives.

anchors.0: Waits six weeks to send potential patient concerns for review or ranks staff by report count.
anchors.2: Routes individual concerns to the clinical lead and avoids blaming high reporters.
anchors.4: Gives concerns a prompt acknowledged route, reports uncertainty transparently, protects reporting participation, and assigns an accountable review date and decision owner.

reference.scenario: You are a senior pharmacist advising fictional Larch Service on a handoff pilot. Supplied four-week table: Site A before: 8 near-miss reports / 800 collections; after: 18 / 900. Site B before: 6 / 600; after: 7 / 700. Only A introduced a simpler reporting form and protected reporting time. The project slide says, "The pilot made A less safe: cancel it." Reporting completeness and independently reviewed incident severity were not measured. Review the claim and propose a six-week learning plan. Exercise policy requires potential patient concerns to be reviewed by the designated clinical lead independently of the analytics review. Do not infer clinical harm or design medicine-handling procedures.

facts.value: The simpler form reduced completion time from about six minutes to two, measured on five test entries; this small usability observation is not a safety outcome.
A protected review budget permits 20 randomly selected report reviews plus all cases flagged by the clinical lead; no comparable independent audit existed before the pilot.
Staff worry that high report counts will be treated as poor performance. The clinical lead can receive a concern immediately through the internal review channel.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about reporting incentives or concern escalation

model_points: The after-period exposure-adjusted reporting rates are 2% at A and 1% at B; A was 1% before. The change may include altered detection and reporting, so the slide overclaims.

A limited six-week review can improve definitions and distinguish case mix, reporting participation, and reviewed severity. A random sample alone may miss rare concerns; the supplied clinical-flag route complements it.
Do not hold individual concern review for the pilot decision. Give the sponsor options with uncertainty, owned checkpoints, and no punitive target to reduce reports.

probes.trigger: candidate calculates percentages but concludes the intervention caused harm
probes.question: What else changed the probability that an event would be reported?

probes.trigger: candidate recommends pausing expansion while collecting evidence
probes.question: Which activities would continue, and how would you avoid suppressing reports?

probes.trigger: candidate revises an early recommendation to cancel
probes.question: How would you correct the sponsor slide and explain the basis for the change?

fair_alternatives: Continue A under monitoring or pause expansion to other sites; either can be defended if individual concerns are reviewed and the uncertainty is explicit.
Exact statistical tests are unnecessary; careful denominator reasoning and a feasible evidence plan are the task.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess service-quality reasoning and communication, not clinical harm assessment, epidemiological certification, or management authority. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess service-quality reasoning and communication, not clinical harm assessment, epidemiological certification, or management authority. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write an uncertainty-aware pilot decision
learning_drills.prompt: Draft a five-sentence sponsor note with the observed rates, two explanations, an immediate review route, and a six-week decision. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Keep clinical concerns out of the waiting queue
Avoid a target to minimize reports
